newsitem.title: CANADA: China rumored Canadian wheat buy seen low - trade.
newsitem.headline: China rumored Canadian wheat buy seen low - trade.

text.p: Rumours that China bought 700,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat for September to December shipment may be low, export sources said.
"There's no question the (Canadian Wheat) Board would have to sell 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes of wheat to the Chinese. We would regard it as a bearish tonnage, it's not enough," one source said.
The CWB sold 800,000 of wheat to China in August, Asian sources said. The latest rumoured sale would bring Canadian exports to at least 1.5 million in 1996/97 (Aug/July).
"I can't confirm that," CWB spokesman Brian Stacey said.
That's up 22 percent from last year's output of 19.12 million tonnes.
"I heard they put a big export program on and there's problems getting canola allocations," a third source said.
All sources said a price of US$210 a tonne, cost and freight, basis Canada's West Coast seemed high.
"I think US$210 C&F sounds far too high priced. I doubt it would be any more than US$200. It might be US$195," one source said.
"US$210 seems like a pretty good price at today's market. If the Board achieved that level they should be very happy," another source said.
Rising world wheat supply should weigh on prices, he said.

"French wheat's collapsing, Argentine's going down and the Americans can't get around the TCK problem and they're trying to sow the seeds of doubt in the Chineses' mind about the quality of Canadian wheat," he added.
